title: MJO simulation in CMIP5 climate models: MJO skill metrics and process-oriented diagnosis
problem: Most climate models struggle to realistically simulate the Madden-Julian Oscillation, underestimating its amplitude and propagating it too quickly, because the specific physical process parameterizations causing these shortcomings are poorly understood, hindering model improvement.
method: This study applies MJO skill metrics and process-oriented diagnostics to 37 CMIP5 climate models to assess their ability to simulate the MJO and to link simulation skill with key parameterized physical processes like moisture-convection coupling and gross moist stability.
task: The task is to assess the Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) simulation skill in 37 CMIP5 models and to establish a link between this skill and specific parameterized physical processes using process-oriented diagnostics.
innovation: This paper assesses Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO) simulation skill in 37 CMIP5 models, using process-oriented diagnostics to establish a link between model performance and the representation of physical processes, particularly moisture-convection coupling and gross moist stability, to guide model improvement.

In observations, the MJO rainfall signal propagates from Indian Ocean to Western Pacific, whereas many CMIP5 models fail to produce coherent eastward propagation of MJO rainfall signal compared to observations.

The CMIP5 models are validated against daily rainfall analyses from the Global Precipitation Climatology Project (GPCP; Huffman et al. 2001) for 1997–2010 and the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM 3B42 version 6; Huffman et al. 2007) for 1998-2010, outgoing longwave radiation (OLR) from the Advanced Very High Resolution Radiometer (AVHRR; Liebmann and Smith 1996) for 1985-2004 and the Clouds and the Earth's Radiant Energy System (CERES; Loeb et al. 2009) for 2001-2010, specific humidity, air temperature, geopotential height, pressure velocity from the ECMWF Reanalysis (ERA-interim; Dee et al. 2011) for 1985–2004, upper (250 hPa) and lower (850 hPa) tropospheric zonal winds (U250 and U850 hereafter) from the ECMWF Reanalysis and the NCEP-NCAR reanalysis (Kalnay et al. 1996) for 1985–2004.
